person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: We hypothesized that attitudes characterized by a strong association between the attitude object and an evaluation of that object are capable of being activated from memory automatically upon mere presentation of the attitude object.

span.label: automatic activation of attitudes
span.quote: The essential question to be addressed is whether attitudes are capable of being activated automatically upon the individual's encountering the attitude object.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: We used a priming procedure to examine the extent to which the mere presentation of an attitude object would facilitate the latency with which subjects could indicate whether a subsequently presented target adjective had a positive or a negative connotation.

span.label: In Experiments 1 and 2 associative strength was measured rather than manipulated, so the two classes of attitude may differ in other ways.
span.quote: Nevertheless, as is the case any time a conceptual variable is measured rather than manipulated, other differences might exist between the two classes of attitudes that were identified via our measurement technique.

span.label: The inhibition produced by weak negative primes in Experiment 1 did not replicate in the later experiments.
span.quote: However, this effect should be interpreted cautiously because, unlike the effect observed for strong primes, it does not replicate in the later experiments to be reported.

span.label: The control primes of Experiment 3 were not equivalent to the weak primes of the first two experiments.
span.quote: Due to the selection requirement concerning unanimity, the control attitude objects in Experiment 3 involved stronger evaluative associations than did the weak primes in Experiments 1 and 2.

span.label: Whether the priming procedure works as an unobtrusive attitude measure has not been tested.
span.quote: Whether the present technique is actually useful in measuring attitudes concerning objects or issues for which self-reports might be suspect remains to be tested.

span.label: automatic activation
span.quote: Apparently, facilitation in the present task is the result of automatic activation of the evaluation upon presentation of the attitude object. However, such automatic activation requires the existence of a strong association

span.label: attitude
span.quote: However, the likelihood of such automatic activation of an attitude appears to depend upon the strength of the association between the attitude object and the evaluation

span.label: associative strength
span.quote: Regardless of whether this associative strength was measured or manipulated experimentally, evidence of automatic activation of the attitude was far stronger when the association could be characterized as strong

span.label: nonattitude
span.quote: These associations can vary in strength, ranging from not existing at all (the case of a nonattitude) to a weak association that is unlikely to be capable of automatic activation to a strong association that can be activated automatically

span.label: AN ATTITUDE BECOMES A QUANTITY WITH A NAMED ZERO: `attitudes as EVALUATIVE ASSOCIATIONS WITH OBJECTS. These associations can VARY IN STRENGTH, ranging from NOT EXISTING AT ALL (the case of a NONATTITUDE) to a weak association that is UNLIKELY to be capable of automatic activation to a strong association that CAN be activated automatically.` **An attitude stops being something a person has or lacks and becomes a link with a magnitude.** Everything else in the paper follows: if it is an association, its strength is measurable, manipulable, and predictive of whether it fires unbidden - and `nonattitude` gives the theory a prediction at the bottom of the scale as well as the top
span.quote: These associations can vary in strength, ranging from not existing at all (the case of a nonattitude) to a weak association that is unlikely to be capable of automatic activation to a strong association that can be activated automatically

span.label: A FIFTH KIND OF BOUNDARY CONDITION - A PROPERTY OF THE STORED REPRESENTATION: `the likelihood of such automatic activation of an attitude appears to DEPEND UPON THE STRENGTH OF THE ASSOCIATION between the attitude object and the evaluation.` The corpus now holds five places a priming effect can be conditional: the OUTCOME SITUATION (ambiguity - four papers), the OBSERVER (prime visibility, Holcomb2005), the STIMULUS (contains a face, Huang2018), the RELATION between primes (conflict, buchner2003), and here **the stored representation itself**. Each needs a different remedy when a replication fails - change the task, screen the subjects, change the materials, redesign the trial structure, or select the items
span.quote: However, the likelihood of such automatic activation of an attitude appears to depend upon the strength of the association between the attitude object and the evaluation

span.label: THE MODERATOR IS BOTH MEASURED AND MANIPULATED, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST FORM THE CLAIM COULD TAKE: `REGARDLESS of whether this associative strength was MEASURED or MANIPULATED EXPERIMENTALLY, evidence of automatic activation of the attitude was FAR STRONGER when the association could be characterized as strong.` Experiments 1 and 2 identified pre-existing strong and weak associations; Experiment 3 created them. **The measured version alone would be confounded with anything that makes an object memorable or familiar; the manipulation rules that out, and the agreement between the two is the argument**
span.quote: Regardless of whether this associative strength was measured or manipulated experimentally, evidence of automatic activation of the attitude was far stronger when the association could be characterized as strong

span.label: AND THE PAPER CLAIMS AFFECT WORKS LIKE MEANING, EXPLICITLY: `they indicate that affect can be activated automatically from memory IN THE SAME WAY THAT HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED PREVIOUSLY FOR SEMANTIC KNOWLEDGE.` **A bridge between two literatures, stated by the paper itself** - the semantic priming of meyer1971 and neely1977 and the affective priming this paper starts are claimed to be one mechanism running on different contents. `Just as activation can spread from one node in the network to another ... the present data indicate a spontaneous spreading of activation from the object to the affective association`
span.quote: they indicate that affect can be activated automatically from memory in the same way that has been demonstrated previously for semantic knowledge

span.label: builds-on → Fazio, Chen, McDonel & Sherman (1982), Fazio, Powell & Herr (1983) and Powell & Fazio (1984) on attitudes as object-evaluation associations
span.quote: In a recent series of experiments concerning attitude accessibility, Fazio and his colleagues (Fazio, Chen, McDonel & Sherman, 1982; Fazio, Powell, & Herr, 1983; Powell & Fazio, 1984) proposed that attitudes be viewed as simple associations between a given object and a given evaluation.

span.label: builds-on → Neely's (1977) semantic priming investigation and its short- versus long-SOA pattern
span.quote: This finding is reminiscent of one from Neely's (1977) investigation.

span.label: builds-on → past research employing the repeated attitudinal expression manipulation (Powell & Fazio, 1984)
span.quote: Such a null effect of repeated expression on attitude extremity is consistent with past research that has employed the repeated attitudinal expression manipulation.

span.label: associative strength —causes→ automatic activation
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **THE STRONGEST-EVIDENCED EDGE ON THIS RECORD, BECAUSE THE SPAN CARRIES BOTH OPERATIONS**: `REGARDLESS of whether ... MEASURED or MANIPULATED experimentally`. A correlational moderator would be confounded with familiarity; the manipulation rules that out, and the quote says both were done. Weight 0.9 rather than 0.95 because `evidence ... was far stronger` is a statement about evidence rather than about effect size.
span.quote: Regardless of whether this associative strength was measured or manipulated experimentally, evidence of automatic activation of the attitude was far stronger when the association could be characterized as strong

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: A 2 (strength of association) X 2 (prime valence) X 2 (target valence) analysis of variance was performed on the facilitation scores.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: The analysis revealed that the expected three-way interaction was statistically significant, F(l, 21) = 6.86, p < .02

span.quote: The analysis revealed that the expected three-way interaction was statistically significant, F(l, 21) = 6.86, p < .02
